entities.name: Marcus Lee
observations: Leads the perception team at Ferroline Robotics
Prefers written design documents over long meetings
Owns the release sign-off for the Halberd planner
Studied mechanical engineering at Delft

entities.name: Priya Raghavan
observations: Runs the weekly Kestrel fleet triage every Tuesday
Wrote the original TimescaleDB ingestion pipeline
Mentors two junior engineers on the Sable Vision team
Keeps open office hours on Thursday afternoons

entities.name: Tomas Berg
observations: Works remotely from Gothenburg in the CET timezone
Maintains the Kestrel dashboard frontend
Escalates production incidents to the Northwind Freight account manager
Allergic to peanuts, so team lunches avoid satay

entities.name: Ferroline Robotics
observations: Builds pick-and-place robot cells for warehouse customers
Headquartered in Singapore with a satellite office in Rotterdam
Raised a Series B round of 42 million dollars in March 2025
Runs a four-day engineering week during December

entities.name: Northwind Freight
observations: Largest logistics customer of Ferroline Robotics by contract value
Operates 14 distribution centres across northern Europe
Requires SOC 2 evidence before approving any software rollout
Renews its service contract every February

entities.name: Halberd
observations: Motion planner that sequences pick-and-place grasps for robot cells
Written in Rust with Python bindings for the simulation harness
Replaced a legacy sampling planner that timed out on cluttered bins
Deploys to the cell controller as a signed OTA bundle

entities.name: Kestrel
observations: Web dashboard showing live status for the mobile robot fleet
Streams telemetry over websockets with a five second refresh
Stores fleet telemetry history in TimescaleDB
Has an offline mode that caches the last known fleet state

entities.name: Sable Vision
observations: Calibrates the 3D cameras mounted above each robot cell
Uses a checkerboard target and a bundle adjustment solve
Calibration fails when the warehouse lighting flickers
Exports camera intrinsics as a YAML file consumed by Halberd

entities.name: Telemetry storage decision
observations: Chose TimescaleDB over InfluxDB for fleet telemetry storage
Deciding factor was native SQL support for the existing reporting stack
Accepted a higher storage cost in exchange for simpler backups
Agreed to revisit the choice if telemetry volume exceeds two terabytes

entities.name: TimescaleDB
observations: PostgreSQL extension that adds hypertables for time series data
Compression policy shrinks fleet telemetry after seven days
Continuous aggregates power the weekly utilisation report
Runs on the same Postgres instance as the Kestrel application tables
